english: Let $S$ be the focus of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{9}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{5}=1$ that lies on the positive $x$-axis. For a point $P$ on the ellipse, let $M$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $P$ to the line $y=\dfrac52$. Then the maximum value of $SP+PM$, as $P$ varies on the ellipse, is ______.
hindi: माना कि दीर्घवृत्त $\dfrac{x^{2}}{9}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{5}=1$ की वह नाभि $S$ है जो धनात्मक $x$-अक्ष पर स्थित है। दीर्घवृत्त पर किसी बिन्दु $P$ के लिए, माना $P$ से रेखा $y=\dfrac52$ पर डाले गए लम्ब का पाद $M$ है। तब $P$ के दीर्घवृत्त पर बदलने पर $SP+PM$ का अधिकतम मान ______ है।
solution: Focal distance $SP=a-ex=3-2\cos\theta$; the ellipse lies below $y=\dfrac52$ ($b=\sqrt5<\dfrac52$), so $PM=\dfrac52-\sqrt5\sin\theta$
solution_full: For a point of the ellipse, $SP=e\cdot$ (distance from the directrix $x=\dfrac{9}{2}$) $=\dfrac23\left(\dfrac92-x\right)=3-\dfrac23x=3-2\cos\theta$.
Every point of the ellipse has $y\le\sqrt5<\dfrac52$, so $PM=\dfrac52-y=\dfrac52-\sqrt5\sin\theta$ (no absolute value is needed).
For $A\cos\theta+B\sin\theta$ the range is $\left[-\sqrt{A^{2}+B^{2}},\sqrt{A^{2}+B^{2}}\right]$; here $\sqrt{4+5}=3$. The maximum of $SP+PM$ is $\dfrac{11}{2}+3=\dfrac{17}{2}$.

It is attained when $(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)=-\dfrac13(2,\sqrt5)$, i.e. at $P\left(-2,-\dfrac53\right)$ (an end of the other latus rectum): $SP=\sqrt{16+\dfrac{25}{9}}=\dfrac{13}{3}$, $PM=\dfrac52+\dfrac53=\dfrac{25}{6}$, sum $\dfrac{51}{6}=8.5$.
(The minimum, $\dfrac{11}{2}-3=2.5$, is simply the distance of $S$ from the line, which is why the maximum is the real question.)
originality_note: New: a focal distance plus a distance to a line, which becomes linear in cos and sin only because SP = a - ex, then maximised by the range of A cos + B sin (way 5). Closest known: maximum distance of a point of an ellipse from a line. Different because: the focal distance is not a distance to a line until the focal-distance form is used, and the minimum is trivial while the maximum needs the trigonometric range.
stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, point and curve introduced, conditions complete, one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with sympy and unique; answer matches the plan. Checked that the whole ellipse lies below y = 5/2 (so PM has one sign), that the maximum is attained, and numerically over 200000 points. Changed: No change.
key_step: Replace SP by a - ex = 3 - 2 cos theta so that SP + PM = 11/2 - (2 cos theta + sqrt5 sin theta).
justification: Two ideas linked: focal distance in linear form and the range of a cos + b sin; numerical answer with no options. Comparable to 2025-P2-Q7 (L3), eccentric-angle reasoning on an ellipse.
blueprint_concepts: Range of a.sin(x) + b.cos(x); maximum and minimum

concept_use.Parametric coordinates for Ellipse: P is written as (3 cos theta, sqrt5 sin theta), which turns SP = 3 - 2 cos theta and PM = 5/2 - sqrt5 sin theta into functions of theta.
concept_use.Range of a.sin(x) + b.cos(x); maximum an: The range of 2 cos theta + sqrt5 sin theta is [-3, 3], so the maximum of SP + PM is 11/2 + 3 = 8.5.
